tips.text: Taeguk refers to the source of everything in the universe and the universal law in which everything continuously goes through cycles of creation and destruction.
Pumse Taeguk symbolizes the root principle of universal philosophy and is constructed by applying the truth inherent in Taeguk's yin and yang principles.
Taeguk Chiljang stands for Ga and symbolizes a mountain that embodies the meaning of mass and firmness.

Bumsogi posture is achieved by shifting your weight on your hind leg
and standing low after setting your front foot forward about a foot length from the tip of the big toe to your hind foot.
Raise your heel so only the ball of the front foot touches the ground

The last of the 13 key movements is Jujumsogi.
Jujumsogi posture is achieved by keeping the tops of your feet parallel about two feet length apart, standing low.

We will now look at the moves in succession, connecting each move.
The key moves of Taegukchijang first part consist of
Orun Patangseon Anmakki, Orun Apchagi, and Wen Anmakki,
Wen Patangseon Anmakki, Wen Apchagi, and Orun Anmakki,
Wen Seonnal Godureo Aremakki, and Orun Seonnal Godureo Aremakki.
Shift your weight to your right foot from Jumbijase.
Turn left using the right ball of your foot and assume the Bomsagi posture.
Start the preparatory move for Anmakki while bending your knee using the momentum from Apchagi.
And complete the Momtongmakki.
Move the moment your heel touches the ground, followed by the ball of the forward kicking foot.
Shift your weight to your front leg and at the same time spin your torso clockwise
using the left ball of your foot as an axis to perform the preparatory moves for Patangseon Anmakki.
Then spin and set your foot in line with the direction of progression and complete Patangseon Anmakki.
Shift your weight to your hind leg.
Perform Wen Duikubi by spinning your torso using the left ball of your foot and setting your right foot.

Gawimakki is a technique used to block by transferring and distributing force to both arms.
The Gawimakki and Gawimakki performed in succession is the first move of Taegukjiljang, third part,
and should be repeated twice from the same Sogi posture respectively.
When first performing Gawimakki from Wen Apgubi, perform Oren Aremakki and Wen Anpalmok Pakalmakki.
Then, complete the Wen Apgubi Gawimakki by following it with Wen Aremakki and Oren Anpalmok Pakalmakki in succession.
Next, set your foot with Oren Apgubi, perform Wen Aremakki and Oren Anpalmok Pakalmakki,
and complete Oren Apgubi Gawimakki by performing Oren Aremakki and Wen Anpalmok Pakalmakki.
We will now connect the Gawimakki moves.
Dujumok Chochojirugi.
This move is used to hold and pull an opponent's neck or head
and attack an opponent's face or torso with your knee at the same time.
First, open your hands so they face each other, then pull them down.
It is more effective if you pull your fists down to the ankle of the kicking foot.
When you hold and pull an opponent down,
you can exert more force if you pull your wrists downward.
The pulling down of your opponent and Murubchigi should be performed simultaneously.
